Well, to put it mildly, the review I'm going to write is so that whoever sees and reads it doesn't go through what happened to me. Everyone has their own decisions, but because I kept taking my dog ​​here, I'm now paying for it after he's been gone for six months. In August 2024, I got him pet insurance since he was getting old, thinking it was for the best. What a mistake! Since this clinic was close to my house, I started going. We went about four or five times. My dog ​​had senile dementia and was 18 years old. One day I asked the vet how his health seemed, and she said, "As long as his organs and heart are functioning, well, as if to say, 'As long as he holds on,'" until July 7th of last year when he had a seizure at night. I took him to the emergency room at another clinic. They told me it could be a stroke, a brain tumor, or meningitis. The next day I went back here, and the vet only told me who had treated him before. When she went to examine him, since he was old and The dementia wasn't very still, and she said, "Oh, he won't let me," and of course, she didn't do it. Then she said she'd give him some vitamins, but I don't think they'll do anything. I asked her what she would do in my situation. I was referring to his joints; he couldn't get up, his legs had lost a lot of strength due to age or some other neurological problem—I'll never know. And she said, "If the animal no longer has a quality of life," meaning she meant euthanasia, that's clear. And that was it. The next day I called her crying, wanting to take my dog ​​to be euthanized because I felt he was already suffering, but I'll never know what was wrong with him because the day before she should have told me to do some tests to at least find out what had happened to him that night. Now I only feel guilty for continuing to take him to this clinic and for not having any empathy, not just for me, but for my dog. Even though he was old, he deserved respect and more attention. But it doesn't end there. In the midst of all my pain, during the euthanasia... He mentioned cremation, and I said, "Of course, individually." I told him I'd go get the ashes myself. He said, "They won't bring them to me." He didn't even bother to ask why I didn't know. Now I've had to find out so many things. I could have gone to my dog's wake, and he didn't say a word to me after all the pain I've felt and continue to feel. What a lack of empathy! The last day with my dog, and I didn't even have the chance to be with him in those final moments and keep him company. But now I can't do anything. But to whoever reads this, you know: be careful and ask a lot of questions. You never know. May this serve as a memorial to my life companion, Potter.
